title: We've been building a crypto strategy backtesting tool. Would love some feedback.
author: RobodOfficial

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: first check on Binance futures: are funding and taker fees inside those fills? on short holds they eat most of what the chart shows, and a backtest without them looks great right up until it runs.

replies.author: RobodOfficial
replies.body: Great point, and thanks for highlighting this. We already deduct taker fees and a modeled funding cost in futures backtests. Those hit net PnL; they are not inside the fill price. Historical funding settlements and slippage are areas we are looking to improve. This is exactly the kind of feedback that helps us build a better research platform. Appreciate it!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: netting fees out of PnL gets the totals right but never changes which trades fire. a marginal short that funding turns into a loser still shows up as a trade you'd take, so per-trade stats stay too rosy. on short perp holds I'd bet historical funding moves the picture more than slippage does.

replies.author: RobodOfficial
replies.body:
You’re absolutely right. Net P&L alone doesn’t tell the full story if per-trade statistics still reflect gross results. Historical funding and its timing are important too.  
This is valuable feedback, and we’re taking it seriously as we improve our backtesting engine.  
Would love to get your thoughts on the platform itself if you’re open to trying it out!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: thanks, but I'm the wrong tester for this one, I don't trade crypto. someone who actually holds perp shorts will push the funding side much harder than I could.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks for the clear answer. One thing that would help users on the results page is showing gross and net P&L side by side, with the funding and fees as separate lines, so readers can see how much of the result survives the costs.

replies.author: RobodOfficial
replies.body:
Appreciate the suggestion! We actually show this breakdown in Robod already gross P&L, net P&L after costs, total trading fees, and funding are displayed separately in our backtest results.  
We’d love to get your feedback on the actual experience too. Happy to arrange test access if you’re interested!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Showing the indicators, entry rule, exits and sizing next to the result is a good idea, and the page is honest about “out-of-sample performance is unavailable”. Even so, a 100% win rate on 13 trades over 55 days isn’t enough to judge, and the exit rule includes three safety orders that average down (25% each, at 0.40%, 0.70% and 0.70%), which can hide losses until a strong trend arrives. I’d show the maximum adverse excursion and the worst unrealized drawdown on each trade next to the win rate, and how many of the 13 used safety orders. A held-out period and the number of indicator combinations tried would also help, since four conditions that must all be true can be fitted to a short window. Funding Rate Radar at Cymetica shows perp funding side by side across venues, which is one input for the holding-cost side.
